thread:
maya: Heads up — ACME prod reported that their Private control plane connections started failing after a Windows update. They see repeated mTLS handshake failures, auth errors on our side. stacktrace attached from their side

alex_k: can you paste the client-side error exactly?

maya: customer says: "tls: handshake failure: tls: unsupported_signature_algorithm" on their agent logs. Happening for all nodes behind their corp egress. Started ~2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.

nicole_sre: that string usually means the client cert signature algorithm isn't acceptable to the server (e.g. sha1-signed certs banned). Did they rotate CAs recently?

maya: they did a rollout of an internal CA last week. They say the CA template still uses sha1WithRSAEncryption for signing legacy tokens.

raj_ops: ok — two angles: 1) server rejects signature alg in TLS CertificateVerify (if our server policy disallows SHA1), or 2) client stack advertises only legacy algos and our server can't select a matching sigalg. Need repro.

maya: asked customer for an openssl s_client dump. they returned this (redacted):
```
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.rdwd:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -msg -state
TLS 1.2, ClientHello
... Certificate, TLSv1.2, length = 1024
*** CertificateVerificationError: unsupported signature algorithm
read from 0x...\n
```

alex_k: can we get our side logs for the connection from the control plane LB for those IPs? which source IPs?

maya: their egress IPs are 3.75.120.44 and 3.75.120.45. forwarded packet capture attached.

nicole_sre: pulled logs — server shows: "tls: no suitable signature algorithm (client 3.75.120.44)" around the same time. So server rejected the client CertificateVerify.

raj_ops: next troubleshooting steps: ask customer to show `openssl x509 -in client.pem -text -noout` for the client cert and the issuing CA cert. we need signature algorithm field (Signature Algorithm: sha1WithRSAEncryption or sha256WithRSAEncryption). also check their agent TLS stack (Windows SChannel vs OpenSSL) — SChannel might escalate after KB update.

maya: sent command. customer returned CA cert header: "Signature Algorithm: sha1WithRSAEncryption". client cert also SHA1.

alex_k: that matches. our control plane TLS policy rejects SHA1-signed client certs (security hardening in 2025). So handshake fails during verification.

maya: customer asks for quick workaround — can they bypass?

nicole_sre: short-term: they can generate a new client cert signed by a SHA256 CA, or reissue CA with stronger signature alg. If they cannot rotate immediately, we can add an allowlist entry to relax signature alg check for their tenant — but that requires an enterprise security exception and an audit. Need approval from security.

raj_ops: file a mitigation runbook: 1) reissue CA with sha256, 2) sign new client certs, 3) deploy to agents, 4) restart agent services. Provide sample openssl commands (we sent to customer):
```
# create new CA key
openssl genrsa -out acme-ca.key 4096
openssl req -x509 -new -nodes -key acme-ca.key -sha256 -days 3650 -out acme-ca.pem -subj "/CN=acme-internal-ca"
# issue client cert
openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048
openssl req -new -key client.key -subj "/CN=acme-agent" -out client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in client.csr -CA acme-ca.pem -CAkey acme-ca.key -CAcreateserial -out client.pem -days 365 -sha256
```

maya: customer confirmed they'll try rotate during their maintenance window tonight. asked if we can hold connections open until then.

nicole_sre: also asked them to confirm there is no middlebox rewriting the cert chain or stripping extensions. but in this case the signature algorithm is intrinsic to the cert so middlebox won't change it.

alex_k: created internal ticket and flagged security for exception path if needed.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-1423 created for tenant acme-prod (priority P2). Assigned: nicole_sre, raj_ops.

maya: I'll monitor. assign to me for follow-up and close once their agents report successful connect.

raj_ops: post-mortem notes to include: enforce cert issuance checks in onboarding docs, add a detection alert if any client certs in customer inventory are signed with weak algos, and add troubleshooting KB referencing this signature-alg mismatch.

maya: thanks — will schedule KB write-up after the fix. :white_check_mark:
